mainEntity.name: How can you assess us that quickly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because we have built the finance function for churches enough times to know exactly what to look for, and we have a system for assembling it. The speed is the point. If a firm takes two weeks to send you a proposal, that is a preview of how quickly they will move once you are a client.

mainEntity.name: We are too small for this.

acceptedAnswer.text: The smaller the staff, the more of the finance work the pastor is personally doing, and the more this matters. Small churches are not a lighter version of this problem. They are usually the sharpest version of it, because one person is doing six jobs.

mainEntity.name: How can you guarantee clarity? That sounds subjective.

acceptedAnswer.text: It would be, which is why we defined it as four things you can check yourself on day 30: your books are current and reconciled, your giving and funds and budget versus actual live on one dashboard, your systems are consolidated with a written blueprint, and you can answer any board question from that dashboard in under five minutes. If any one of those is not true, you get a full refund.

mainEntity.name: Our books are badly behind. Is that a problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the normal starting point. We have begun with churches two years behind, and nothing you tell us is going to shock us. Catch-up work is quoted separately based on how far behind the books actually are, and the audit tells you exactly where that stands before you commit to anything.
